key_insight: In thin 316L foil laser keyhole welding, increasing line energy triggers keyhole instability that nucleates holes, which then grow rapidly until the hole length approaches the sheet thickness and perforation occurs.
engineering_relevance: The results define practical energy windows for making continuous seams versus avoiding unintended holes or cutting in thin-sheet laser welding.
method: High-speed imaging of bead-on-plate welding on 200 μm foils to observe keyhole dynamics
Correlation of line energy with keyhole instability, hole nucleation, and growth behavior
Geometric stability assessment using a Young-Laplace force-balance criterion
evidence_signal: The abstract reports continuous seams up to about 7 kJ/m, hole formation above this range, and dominant cutting above about 12 kJ/m, with holes expanding at roughly 0.8–1.2 m/s over 1–3 ms.
watch_item: The stability threshold is geometry- and thickness-dependent, so process windows may change for different foil thicknesses, joint configurations, or alloys.
paper_title: Rupture and growth of holes in the melt pool during laser keyhole welding of thin sheets
